neighbours.label: the 'to' or 'not' after a verb of refusal or of making someone act (refused to, won't, get them to), the slot where a resisted or caused action comes, as against the same sentences with a neutral verb (began to, wanted to, tried to)
fire: At the border, the driver refused to open the trunk.
The only way to calm him down is to get him to breathe slowly.
Despite the warnings, the captain refused to leave the ship.
My sister refused to apologise for what she had said.
The coach managed to get the players to train harder.
When the bill came, he refused to pay for the wine.
The trick with toddlers is to get them to eat vegetables.
The witness refused to answer any more questions.
quiet: At the border, the driver began to open the trunk.
The only way to calm him down is a slow walk outside.
Despite the warnings, the captain decided to stay on deck.
My sister wanted to talk about what she had said.
The coach planned a harder training week for the players.
When the bill came, he offered a toast with the wine.
The trick with toddlers is a small plate of vegetables.
The witness tried to remember more details.
